changes: Group send API types/store now unwrap both 201 message and 207 {message,upload_failures}. Known 207 results are committed sends, including all-files-failed results; they no longer leave the original text as an apparently failed send.

Additive SQLite migration 118 and PostgreSQL migration 020 preserve nullable original file_key_index (0..9). Handler records success/failure indices from multipart order, and repository list/file-URL readers return them. Legacy encrypted_N.bin filenames also resolve original key positions rather than compacted/tied database order; other legacy names retain positional fallback.

Group attachment rendering and exact-version cache checks use the same key resolver. A failed earlier upload or changed row ordering cannot silently select a different modern file key. Missing/invalid indices fail closed.

Failed original File objects are kept in an account/group-owned in-memory recovery list. Explicit retry re-encrypts only these files into a new current-membership message with empty original text. Duplicate retry clicks are locked; another partial result creates a new recovery entry, while a failed retry retains the original one.

Unverifiable failure positions are not automatically retried. Explicit review restores files alongside a newer composer draft, with per-file removal and a warning about already-uploaded files. Recovery dismiss is explicit; account change and membership removal clear recovery references. No disk plaintext persistence or automatic retry was added.

Upload service bounds bytes actually copied, records actual ciphertext size and removes new test/upload files on failure. Attachment insert timestamp read-back is best-effort after a committed row, preventing false partial failure and removal of a successfully persisted file.
Group recovery/file UI has localized labels and fixed grid rows so optional call/error/recovery sections do not consume the message area's minmax track. Send/edit/review clear superseded error state.
verification: Full Linux Docker server CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./... -timeout=15m passed, including repository 43.851s / services 21.292s. Covers both new embedded migrations on fresh SQLite test databases.

PostgreSQL 18 affected repository/handler/service tests passed (1.500s / 0.239s / 0.247s) with fresh disposable schemas. Tests cover nullable legacy rows, explicit/sparse index round-trip, file-URL lookup, CHECK constraint and a committed insert with deliberately failed timestamp read-back.

HTTP tests cover first-file failure, all-files failure and full success: exactly one message save/broadcast, original success/failure key indices and 201/207 envelopes. Upload service tests cover actual bytes vs header hints, hard size limit, invalid index and metadata failure cleanup.

Full client regression: 223 files / 2112 tests passed in 46.76s before the final superseded-error cleanup and added real-crypto case. Final tsc -b and targeted ESLint passed; 5 affected files / 79 tests passed afterward (4.24s).

Client cases verify 207 commit interpretation, failed-files-only empty-text retry, retry locking/failure retention, unknown-index review, newer draft preservation, individual file removal, account cleanup, sparse cached keys and legacy filename resolution.

Real WebCrypto AES-GCM/SHA-256 test opens the successful second file through its original index, rejects the wrong first key, re-encrypts the failed first file with a different key/IV, opens that retry and rejects its old key. This is local crypto integration, not real two-client/media acceptance.

OpenAPI parses with 221 paths and zero unresolved internal refs; group message multipart, 201/207 envelopes and index bounds are documented. An initially mistyped rate-limit response reference was fixed to the existing TooManyRequestsError.

Final local Vite production web build passed (1647 modules, 686ms); existing config-loader/chunk/dynamic-import warnings remain unsuppressed. Temporary no-host-port PostgreSQL QA container was stopped; existing browser QA backend was left running.
remaining: Network timeout/connection-loss outcomes are not solved by parsing a known 207 result. Group send idempotency/outcome reconciliation is still required before promising duplicate-free unknown-outcome retries.

A changed composer revision during an original pending send deliberately preserves the newer draft; its submitted-file reconciliation still needs acceptance against partial recovery actions. No newer text is silently replaced.

Actual two-client Windows/web upload/decrypt/reconnect, real disk-full and membership-rekey acceptance, 390px/200% layout and screen-reader/touch checks remain unperformed. Ego Lite space is still handed to the user.

Full PostgreSQL regression and production backup/upgrade/rollback rehearsal remain incomplete. Only isolated test schemas applied these migrations. Group partial-upload work does not close P4 or the overall goal.
